scripts.//lint: --concurrency is a FIXED 2 with a 3072 MB heap per V8 isolate, never `auto`. MEMORY, not CPU, sets this number. Both eslint blocks are type-aware (src/** → tsconfig.json, e2e/** → tsconfig.e2e.json). eslint's workers are threads pulling from one shared file queue, so EVERY worker builds its own full src TypeScript program, and memory grows with the workers and with the files each one lints. Node sizes each isolate's heap from the cgroup: 2096 MB in the 8 GB web:lint container (node:22-alpine, measured). Peak container memory on Linux, node 22, over src/ e2e/ playwright*.config.ts (2487 + 348 files, 2026-11-14): 4 workers at the 2096 MB default → OOM-killed at a 7 GB cap after 51s, and 8.6-9.6 GB RSS uncapped on macOS, so it is the exit 137 against the 8 GB cap on the dell runners · 3 @ 2560 → killed at 7 GB · 2 @ 3072 → 5.7 GB peak, passes · 1 @ 4096 → 3.8 GB, but 4.6x slower than 2. Lowering workers WITHOUT raising the heap only swaps the kill for a JS heap OOM: 2 workers need between 2048 and 2560 MB each (2048 fails, 2560 passes), and a single isolate at the default heap also fails. So the heap flag and the worker count are one setting: `lint` and `lint:fix` share it and must be retuned together. Never use `auto`: it resolves to the host CPU count, ignores the cgroup, and multiplies the per-worker TS program by every core. Local macOS wall time on an 18-core host: 4 → 31s · 2 @ 3072 → 50s · off → 60s.
scripts.test:e2e:coverage: VITE_COVERAGE=true npm run build && playwright test && npm run coverage:e2e:merge
scripts.//e2e:schema-report: Measure how much of docs/api/openapi.json the e2e mock layer is actually bound to (#3440). Two steps, because the numbers come from a real run: `TRUEPPM_E2E_SCHEMA_GUARD=report TRUEPPM_E2E_SCHEMA_REPORT=/tmp/schema.ndjson npx playwright test` observes without failing, then this aggregates. `report` mode is for measurement only — CI must never set it, and scripts/check-e2e-schema-guard.sh enforces that.
scripts.//knip:strict: Dead-export gate (#3375), run by the web:knip CI check (web:static job). `--no-config-hints` because two of the `ignore` entries in knip.jsonc name gitignored build artifacts that are absent from a clean checkout, so knip hints to remove them on every CI run — the ignores exist for the working tree that HAS built. Note the name is not `knip --strict`: that flag means something else entirely (consider only direct dependencies, not devDependencies) and would report most of this package's imports as unlisted.
